subproblem.title: Markov choice of r ∈ (ρ/2, ρ) off a null set with ofReal(F′(r)) ≤ (4/ρ)·B (Simon 6.5.1 (10))
subproblem.statement: Let F : ℝ → ℝ be monotone (nondecreasing), let ρ > 0 be real, let B ∈ [0, ∞], and let N ⊆ ℝ be Lebesgue-null (volume N = 0). Suppose ofReal(F(ρ) − F(ρ/2)) ≤ B. Then there is r with ρ/2 < r < ρ and r ∉ N such that ofReal(F′(r)) ≤ ofReal(4/ρ)·B. Here F′ = deriv F (Mathlib's derivative, equal to 0 where F is not differentiable), ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal, and the product is taken in [0, ∞].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (F : ℝ → ℝ) (ρ : ℝ) (B : ℝ≥0∞) (N : Set ℝ), Monotone F → 0 < ρ → ENNReal.ofReal (F ρ - F (ρ / 2)) ≤ B → (volume : Measure ℝ) N = 0 → ∃ r ∈ Ioo (ρ / 2) ρ, r ∉ N ∧ ENNReal.ofReal (deriv F r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (4 / ρ) * B
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5–6 of the supplied proof of the selected node dimred_mbl_dtsd_good_radius, isolated for a general monotone F and an arbitrary Lebesgue-null set N. The book source is Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, (10) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1731–1734): "by 4.10 we know that for each ρ ∈ (0, 1/4) we can find σ ∈ (ρ/2, ρ) such that M⟨T_ρ, d_ρ, σ⟩ ≤ (c/ρ)·M(T_ρ − T_{ρ/2})". The integral bound behind it is the remark before 4.10 (lines 1367–1375). Markov's inequality is the measure-theoretic one (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markov%27s_inequality). Throughout, ofReal := ENNReal.ofReal, λ := volume (Lebesgue measure on ℝ), F′ := deriv F, and
   I := Ioo (ρ/2) ρ, c := ofReal(4/ρ)·B ∈ [0, ∞], g(t) := ofReal(F′(t)), S := {t ∈ I : g(t) ≤ c}.

1. (The interval.) I is measurable (measurableSet_Ioo), and λ(I) = ofReal(ρ − ρ/2) = ofReal(ρ/2) (Real.volume_Ioo). Since ρ > 0, we have ρ/2 > 0 and so λ(I) > 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pos). Also 4/ρ > 0, so ofReal(4/ρ) > 0.

2. (Integral bound.) g is measurable: deriv F is measurable (measurable_deriv), and so is its composition with ENNReal.ofReal (Measurable.ennreal_ofReal). Apply the sibling cmcs_smi_lintegral_ofReal_deriv_le (key lebesgue_deriv) with a = ρ/2 and b = ρ; F is monotone. It gives ∫⁻_I g dλ ≤ ofReal(F(ρ) − F(ρ/2)), and this is ≤ B by hypothesis. So ∫⁻_I g dλ ≤ B.

3. (Covering inequality.) Every t ∈ I lies in S or in I \ S, so I ⊆ S ∪ (I \ S). Hence λ(I) ≤ λ(S ∪ (I \ S)) ≤ λ(S) + λ(I \ S) (measure_mono, measure_union_le).

4. (λ(S) > 0.) There are three cases.
   (a) B = ∞. Then c = ofReal(4/ρ)·∞ = ∞, because ofReal(4/ρ) ≠ 0 (ENNReal.mul_top). Every t ∈ I satisfies g(t) ≤ ∞ = c. So S = I, and λ(S) = λ(I) > 0 by step 1.
   (b) B = 0. Then c = ofReal(4/ρ)·0 = 0. By step 2, ∫⁻_I g dλ ≤ 0, so ∫⁻_I g dλ = 0. Since g is measurable, lintegral_eq_zero_iff gives g = 0 almost everywhere for λ⌞I = volume.restrict I. That is, λ⌞I({t : g(t) ≠ 0}) = 0 (ae_iff), i.e. λ({t : g(t) ≠ 0} ∩ I) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply' with I measurable). If t ∈ I \ S, then g(t) ≤ 0 = c fails, so g(t) ≠ 0. Thus I \ S ⊆ {t : g(t) ≠ 0} ∩ I, and λ(I \ S) = 0 (measure_mono_null). Step 3 then gives λ(I) ≤ λ(S) + 0, so λ(S) ≥ λ(I) > 0.
   (c) 0 < B < ∞. Apply Markov's inequality to the measure λ⌞I and the measurable function g (mul_meas_ge_le_lintegral₀): c·λ⌞I({t : c ≤ g(t)}) ≤ ∫⁻_I g dλ. Put E := {t : c ≤ g(t)} ∩ I; then λ⌞I({c ≤ g}) = λ(E) (Measure.restrict_apply'). With step 2, c·λ(E) ≤ B. By commutativity and associativity, c·λ(E) = B·(ofReal(4/ρ)·λ(E)), so B·(ofReal(4/ρ)·λ(E)) ≤ B·1. Since B ≠ 0 and B ≠ ∞, B cancels (ENNReal.mul_le_mul_iff_right): ofReal(4/ρ)·λ(E) ≤ 1. Hence λ(E) ≤ (ofReal(4/ρ))⁻¹ (ENNReal.le_inv_iff_mul_le). Moreover (ofReal(4/ρ))⁻¹ = ofReal((4/ρ)⁻¹) = ofReal(ρ/4) (ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos with 4/ρ > 0; inv_div). If t ∈ I \ S, then g(t) ≤ c fails, so c < g(t); in particular c ≤ g(t) and t ∈ E. Hence I \ S ⊆ E and λ(I \ S) ≤ λ(E) ≤ ofReal(ρ/4). Now suppose, for contradiction, that λ(S) = 0. Step 3 gives ofReal(ρ/2) = λ(I) ≤ 0 + ofReal(ρ/4) = ofReal(ρ/4). Since ρ/4 ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff gives ρ/2 ≤ ρ/4, contradicting ρ > 0. Hence λ(S) > 0.

5. (Avoiding the null set.) Since λ(N) = 0, λ(S \ N) = λ(S) (measure_sdiff_null; N need not be measurable), and this is > 0 by step 4. A set of nonzero measure is nonempty (nonempty_of_measure_ne_zero), so there is r ∈ S \ N.

6. (Conclusion.) For this r: r ∈ S ⊆ I, so ρ/2 < r < ρ. Also r ∉ N, and ofReal(deriv F r) = g(r) ≤ c = ofReal(4/ρ)·B by definition of S. ∎
proof_key_steps: I := (ρ/2, ρ) has λ(I) = ofReal(ρ/2) > 0; g := ofReal ∘ deriv F is measurable; c := ofReal(4/ρ)·B; S := {t ∈ I : g t ≤ c}.
∫⁻_I g ≤ ofReal(F(ρ) − F(ρ/2)) ≤ B by the sibling cmcs_smi_lintegral_ofReal_deriv_le and the hypothesis.
λ(S) > 0: if B = ∞ then c = ∞ and S = I; if B = 0 then g = 0 a.e. on I, so I \ S is null; if 0 < B < ∞ then Markov gives λ(I \ S) ≤ ofReal(ρ/4) < ofReal(ρ/2) = λ(I).
λ(S \ N) = λ(S) > 0, so pick r ∈ S \ N.
